findings.what: The step from v × i to '1000 W × the sine squared' is skipped on screen; add 100 sin × 10 sin = 1000 sin² so the fold's starting point comes from the multiplication he has just watched.

'Averaging the voltage and the current first throws away the backward half' misdescribes it: averaging first lets the backward half cancel the forward half, whereas in the product the backward half heats just as well; reword to say that.
'Meters read rms values' is flat and absolute; say the clamp meter shows an rms value (lesson 2) and the 230 V is rms.

findings.where: Screen 4 task ('Most ships run at 60 Hz') and screen 9 text ('the supply most ships use')
findings.what: The source says 60 Hz is 'the most common frequency adopted for use on board ship'; keep to those words, as the explain text already does.
Stray punctuation: 'Its power is 230 × 10 = 2300 W,.' should end '= 2300 W.'.
The text opens 'Switch to 60 Hz' while the demonstration does the switching itself; say 'Watch the supply switch to 60 Hz', then invite him to switch back and forth.

findings.where: All screens, light mode, graph colours and key
findings.what: The voltage wave (ink) and the power wave (accent2) are near-identical dark navy in light mode, so their key swatches and the voltage and power dots on the cursor look the same; they sit on separate graphs, so this does not mislead, but a clearer tint for power would help.

findings.where: Every screen at 360 px, lead paragraph and screen 1 text
findings.what: The six-line lead repeats above every screen, and screen 1's paragraph runs to about twelve lines, so the picture starts near the bottom of a phone screen; shorten the lead to one line and trim screen 1.

230 V × 10 A = 2300 W is answerable from his trade alone; screen 12 asks the same thing with the hump count added, so screen 8 could also ask for the hump top (4600 W, for an instant) to test what is new.
'The same look' glosses one difference: the rectifier's humps meet zero in sharp points while a sine squared touches zero smoothly; one clause in 'breaks' would make it exact.
The picture is capped at 22rem inside a wider column, so on a laptop the graphs and 13 px labels are smaller than they need to be; let it widen to the column.
